questions.question: Four friends, Priya, Kavya, Gaurvi and Shalini, have different amounts of money with them. If Priya takes ₹88 from Kavya, then she will have an amount equal to what Gaurvi has. Shalini and Kavya together have a total of ₹550. If Gaurvi takes ₹25 from Shalini, she will have an amount equal to what Kavya has. If the total amount with Shalini, Kavya and Gaurvi is ₹840, how much money does Priya have?
questions.questionHtml: Four friends, Priya, Kavya, Gaurvi and Shalini, have different amounts of money with them. If Priya takes ₹88 from Kavya, then she will have an amount equal to what Gaurvi has. Shalini and Kavya together have a total of ₹550. If Gaurvi takes ₹25 from Shalini, she will have an amount equal to what Kavya has. If the total amount with Shalini, Kavya and Gaurvi is ₹840, how much money does Priya have?
questions.solution:
Given:

Equation (1) → Priya takes ₹88 from Kavya, then she will have an amount equal to what Gaurvi has.

Priya + 88 = Gaurvi

Equation (2) → Shalini and Kavya together have a total of ₹550.

Shalini + Kavya = 550

Equation (3) → If Gaurvi takes ₹25 from Shalini, she will have an amount equal to what Kavya has.

Gaurvi + 25 = Kavya

Equation (4) → Total amount with Shalini, Kavya and Gaurvi is ₹840.

Shalini + Kavya + Gaurvi = 840

From equation (4) and (2)

Gaurvi  + 550 = 840

Gaurvi = 840 – 550 = 290

From equation (1) → Priya + 88 = Gaurvi

So, Priya + 88 = 290

Priya = 290 – 88 = 202

Hence, Priya have ‘202’ rs.

Key Points

  • A Conservative force is a force with the property that the total work done in a moving particle between two points is independent of the path taken.
    • Conservative force depends only on the position of the particle.
    • The force is independent of the path
    • Examples of conservative forces are Gravitational force, Spring force, Magnetic force and Electric force.
  • On the other hand, non-conservative forces are those forces that cause the loss of mechanical energy from the system.
    • But as we know that energy can neither be created nor destroyed so these forces convert mechanical energy into heat, sound, light etc.
    • The force depends on the path.
    • Examples of non-conservative forces are friction, air resistance, and tension in the cord.

questions.question: ______ is the water transporting tissue in plants.
questions.questionHtml: ______ is the water transporting tissue in plants.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Xylem.

  • Xylem is the water transporting tissue in plants.​

Key Points

  • Xylem is one of two types of transport tissue in vascular plants.
    • The basic function of the xylem is to transport water from the root to the stem and leaves, but it also transports nutrients.
    • The term xylem was introduced by Carl Nagelei in 1858, derived from an ancient Greek word meaning wood.

Additional Information 

  • Phloem is the living tissue in vascular plants that transports soluble organic compounds formed during photosynthesis and known as photosynthesis, especially the sugar sucrose, to parts of the plant where needed. This transport process is called transfer.
  • In a vascular plant, the stele is the central part of the root or stem containing the tissues derived from the procambium.
  • The cortex is the outer layer of the stem or root in a plant, which lies beneath the epidermis but outside the vascular bundles. It is responsible for transporting material to the central cylinder of the root via diffusion and can also be used for food storage in the form of starch.

questions.question: A can do a piece of work in 2 days, and B can do five times the same work in 15 days when they work for ten hours a day. If they work together, then how many hours in addition to a day's work will they require to complete the work?
questions.questionHtml: A can do a piece of work in 2 days, and B can do five times the same work in 15 days when they work for ten hours a day. If they work together, then how many hours in addition to a day's work will they require to complete the work?
questions.solution:
Work = Efficiency × Time

B complete the same work as A do = 15/5 = 5days 

Work of A : Work of B = 2 : 3

Efficiency of A : Efficiency of B = 3 : 2 

A work for ten hours a day = (2 × 10) = 20 

B works for ten hours a day = (3 × 10) = 30

Total work = LCM of 20 and 30 = 60

Time taken by A and B together  = [60/(3 + 2)]

⇒ (60/5) ⇒ 12 hrs

Hours in addition to a day's work = 12 - 10 = 2 hrs

The six digit number = 823p2q

Concept used:

Divisibility rule of  7 - The difference between twice the unit digit of the given number and the remaining part of the given number should be a multiple of 7 or it should be equal to 0.

Divisibility rule of 11 - If the difference between the sum of the digits at the odd and even places equals 0 or divisible by 11, then the number is divisible by 11.

Divisibility rule of 13 -  A number is divisible by 13 when the ones place digit of a number is multiplied by 4 and the product is added to the rest of the number either gives 0 or a multiple of 13.

7 × 11 × 13 = 1001, when any three digit number multiplied by 1001 then it repeats itself and always completely divisible by 7, 11 and 13.

compare both sides

⇒ p = 8, q = 3

By comparing both number, p = 8 and q = 3

Now,

Required value = (p – q) = (8 – 3)

⇒ 5

∴ The required value is 5.

Given:

The average weight of a certain number of students in a class = 55.5 kg

4 students with average weight 60 kg join the class, the average weight of all students in the class increases by 360 g (0.360 Kg). 

Formula used:

Average = sum of observations/Number of observations

Calculation:

Let the number of students initially be x.

Sum = Average × Number of students

Total initial weight = 55.5x kg

Weight of new students = (4 × 60) = 240 kg

The new average = 55.5 + 0.360 = 55.86

questions.question: The marked price of an article is Rs. 5320. It is subject to two successive discounts, the first being 15%, and the second at a rate of 20% of the first. What is the selling price (to nearest Rs.) of the article?
questions.questionHtml: The marked price of an article is Rs. 5320. It is subject to two successive discounts, the first being 15%, and the second at a rate of 20% of the first. What is the selling price (to nearest Rs.) of the article?
questions.solution:
Given:

The marked price = Rs. 5320

Two successive discounts = 15%, and the second at a rate of 20% of the first.

Formula used:

Single discount on two successive discounts = (a + b – ab/100)

Calculation:

Let the selling price be 100

According to the question

The second at a rate of 20% of the first = (20% of 15)

⇒ (20/100 × 15) = 3%

Now, single discount on two successive discount = (a + b – ab/100)

⇒ (15 + 3 – 15 × 3/100)

⇒ (18 – 0.45) = 17.55%

Now, (100 – 17.55)% = 82.45%

Selling price = (82.45% of 5320)

⇒ (82.45/100 × 5320)

⇒ (438634/100)

⇒ Rs. 4386.34 ~ Rs. 4386

∴ The required selling price is Rs. 4386

Mistake PointsNote the language of the question

"second at a rate of 20% of the first " which means 20% of 15 = 3%.

Don't take the second discount = 20 %. 

Alternate MethodGiven that, the marked price is Rs. 5320

According to the question

The second at a rate of 20% of the first = (20% of 15)

⇒ (20/100 × 15) = 3%

Hence, the selling price 

SP =  \(5320× (1-\frac{15}{100})(1-\frac{3}{100})\)

⇒ SP = (5320 × 85 × 97)/10000

⇒ SP = 4386

Downstream = u + v

Upstream = u – v

questions.question: AB is a chord of a circle with centre O and P is any point on the circle. If ∠APB = 122°, then what is the measure of ∠OAB ?
questions.questionHtml: AB is a chord of a circle with centre O and P is any point on the circle. If ∠APB = 122°, then what is the measure of ∠OAB ?
questions.solution:
Given:

∠APB = 122° 

Concept used:

Sum of opposite sides of a cyclic quadrilateral are 180°

The angle subtended by an arc of a circle at its center is twice the angle it subtends anywhere on the circle’s circumference.

Calculation:

In the given figure,

APBT is a cyclic quadrilateral.

∠ATB + ∠APB = 180° [sum of opposite angles are 180°]

⇒ x° + 122° = 180° 

⇒ x = (180° – 122°)

⇒ x = 58° 

∠ATB = 58° 

And we know that the angle subtended by an arc of a circle at its center is twice the angle it subtends anywhere on the circle’s circumference.

⇒ ∠AOB = 2 × ∠ATB

⇒ ∠AOB = 2 × 58° 

⇒ ∠AOB = 116° 

Now,

OA = OB [radius of the circle]

Then,

∠OAB + ∠AOB + ∠OBA = 180° 

⇒ θ + 116° + θ = 180° 

⇒ 2θ + 116° = 180° 

⇒ 2θ = (180° – 116°)

⇒ 2θ = 64° 

⇒ θ = 32° 

so,

∠OAB = θ = 32° 

∴ The required value of ∠OAB is 32°.

Shortcut Trick 

From the above given diagram we have

⇒ θ = P - 90°

⇒ θ = 122° - 90° = 32°

∴ The correct answer is 32°.

questions.question: Directions: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. One of / the biggest enterprise / in India / is declaring a lockout.
questions.questionHtml:
Directions: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

One of / the biggest enterprise / in India / is declaring a lockout.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'the biggest enterprise' i.e. this part of the sentence has an error.

Key Points

  • In the given sentence, the singular form of the noun ''enterprise'' is incorrect.
  • The phrase ''One of'' in the given sentence is a singular term and is generally used to talk about a noun or a pronoun.
  • The noun or a pronoun used after the phrase ''one of'' is always in the plural form (as we are talking of one person/place/thing out of many).
  • Therefore, the plural form of the noun ''enterprises'' should be used in place of the singular noun 'enterprise'.
  • Also, the helping verb will always be in the singular form (here, is), as the helping verb agrees with ''one of'' and not with the plural noun in the sentence.
     

Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

Correct sentence: One of the biggest enterprises in India is declaring a lockout.

Additional Information

  • Subjects and verbs must agree with one another in number (singular or plural). (विषय और क्रिया एक दूसरे के साथ संख्या (एकवचन या बहुवचन) में सहमत होना चाहिए)
  • Thus, if a subject is singular, its verb must also be singular; if the subject is plural, its verb must also be plural. (इस प्रकार, यदि कोई विषय एकवचन है , तो उसकी क्रिया भी एकवचन होनी चाहिए ; यदि विषय बहुवचन है , तो उसकी क्रिया भी बहुवचन होनी चाहिए)
     

Hinglish

  • दिए गए वाक्य में noun ''enterprise'' का एकवचन रूप गलत है।
  • दिए गए वाक्य में phrase ''One of'' एकवचन शब्द है और आमतौर पर संज्ञा या सर्वनाम के बारे में बात करने के लिए प्रयोग किया जाता है।
  • Phrase ''one of'' के बाद प्रयुक्त संज्ञा या सर्वनाम हमेशा बहुवचन रूप में होता है (जैसा कि हम कई में से एक व्यक्ति/स्थान/वस्तु की बात कर रहे हैं)।
  • इसलिए एकवचन noun 'enterprise' के स्थान पर बहुवचन noun ''enterprises'' का प्रयोग किया जाना चाहिए।

questions.questionHtml:
Directions: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. Sculpture and painting form an integral part of temple architecture.

B. The city is visited by thousands curious to see the temple in the form of a chariot.

C. The finest example of this is Konark Temple in Puri.

The correct answer is 'ACBD.'

Key Points

  • The sentence 'A' is independent of any other sentence as it is giving general information about "temple architecture". Hence, 'A' is the first part.
  • Sentence C will come after A as it is giving information about the finest example of temple architecture (Konark Temple in Puri).
  • Sentence B will come after C as it is giving information about the curiosity behind the visit of thousands of people to the city 'Puri'.
  • The sentence 'D' is the concluding part as it is giving information about the material used to carve the chariot-shaped temple.
     

Paragraph after rearranging the sentences: Sculpture and painting form an integral part of temple architecture. The finest example of this is Konark Temple in Puri. The city is visited by thousands curious to see the temple in the form of a chariot. The chariot with immense wheels and horses is carved from stone.

Hint

  • Important Rules to Solve the Para Jumbles:
    • Read the sentences attentively and try to comprehend the idea or theme of the sentence and eliminate the irrelevant options.
    • Try to identify the opening (independent sentence) and closing sentences (concluding sentence).
    • Try to identify the mandatory pairs. Two sentences can be connected through various connectors and other determinants.

The correct answer is The French scientist said that he wanted to study how bees and wasps found their way home.

Key Points

  • The given sentence is a direct speech.
  • The basic rules for changing or converting direct speech into indirect speech:​
    • The commas, inverted commas are removed, and 'that' is added.
    • The first-person pronoun ''I'' becomes the third-person pronoun ''he''.
    • The present simple tense format 'Subject + V1 (want) + Object' will be changed into the past simple tense format 'Subject + V2 (wanted) + Object'.
    • The present simple tense format 'Subject + V1 (find) + Object' will be changed into the past simple tense format 'Subject + V2 (found) + Object'.
       

Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

Additional Information

  • The following table will enable us to know how tense changes into Indirect speech:-
    Direct Speech Indirect Speech
    Present simple (Subject +V1st + Object) Past simple (Subject +V2 + Object)
    Present continuous (Subject +is/am/are+V1 +ing+ Object) Past Continuous (Subject +was/were+V1 +ing+ Object)
    Present perfect (Subject + has/have+V3+Object) Past perfect (Subject+had+V3+Object)
    Past simple (Subject+V2+Object) Past perfect (Subject+had+V3+Object)
    Past Continuous (Subject +was/were+V1+ing+ Object) Past perfect continuous (Subject+had been+V1 +ing+ Object)
    Future simple (Subject+ will/shall+V1+object) Present Conditional (Subject+would+V1+object)
    Future Continuous (Subject +will/shall+be+V1 +ing+ Object) Conditional Continuous (Subject +would+be+V1 +ing+ Object)

 

Hinglish

  • दिया गया वाक्य direct speech है।
  • Direct speech को indirect speech में बदलने या बदलने के लिए बुनियादी नियम:
    • Commas, inverted commas हटा दिए जाते हैं और 'that' जोड़ा जाता है।
    • The first-person pronoun ''I'', third-person pronoun ''he'' बन जाता है।
    • Present simple tense format 'Subject + V1 (want) + Object' को past simple tense format 'Subject + V2 (wanted) + Object' में बदल दिया जाएगा।
    • Present simple tense format 'Subject + V1 (find) + Object' को past simple tense format 'Subject + V2 (found) + Object' में बदल दिया जाएगा।

questions.question: Directions: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select ‘No substitution’. The shopkeeper would have fined her if he come to know that she damaged the toy on exhibit.
questions.questionHtml:
Directions: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select ‘No substitution’.

The shopkeeper would have fined her if he come to know that she damaged the toy on exhibit.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'he had come to know.'

Key Points

  • In the underlined segment, the use of the simple present form of the verb ''come'' is incorrect.
  • The given sentence is the third conditional sentence explaining that present circumstances would be different if something different had happened in the past.
  • The third conditional sentence structure is as follows:
    • If + past perfect..., + conditional perfect (would + have + past participle).
    • Conditional perfect (would + have + past participle) + if + past perfect.
  • When using the third conditional, we use the past perfect (i.e., had + past participle) in the if-clause and the modal auxiliary (would, could, should, etc.) + have + past participle in the main clause.
  • Therefore, the past perfect form of the verb ''had come'' should be used in place of the simple present form of the verb 'come'.
     

Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

Correct sentence: The shopkeeper would have fined her if he had come to know that she damaged the toy on exhibit.

Mistake Points

  • Do not get confused between the present and past forms of the verb 'come'.
  • Here are the correct forms of come:-
1st form (Base form) 2nd form (Past form) 3rd form (Past Participle form)
Come Came Come

Hinglish

  • रेखांकित खण्ड में simple present form of the verb ''come'' का प्रयोग गलत है।
  • दिया गया वाक्य third conditional sentence है जो यह बताता है कि यदि अतीत में कुछ अलग हुआ होता तो वर्तमान परिस्थितियाँ भिन्न होतीं।
  • Third conditional sentence की संरचना इस प्रकार है:
    • If + past perfect..., + conditional perfect (would + have + past participle).
    • Conditional perfect (would + have + past participle) + if + past perfect.
  • Third conditional का उपयोग करते समय, हम if-क्लॉज में past perfect (had + past participle) का उपयोग करते हैं और modal auxiliary (would, could, should, etc.) + have + past participle, main clause में।
  • अतः verb 'come' के simple present form के स्थान पर past perfect form of the verb ''had come'' का प्रयोग किया जाना चाहिए।
     

अतः सही उत्तर option 3 है।

सही वाक्य: The shopkeeper would have fined her if he had come to know that she damaged the toy on exhibit.

Key Points

  • In the underlined segment, the use of the third-person present singular form of the verb 'mends' is incorrect.
  • 'Does' is an auxiliary verb or helping verb that is followed by the main verb.
  • When there is an auxiliary verb, the main verb does not need to be marked for tense, because the tense is shown in the auxiliary.
  • The verb that follows the auxiliary verbs ''do, does, and did'' should be used in its base or root form.
  • When creating negative sentences, we usually use shortened forms: don’t, doesn’t, and didn’t together with the base form of the verb.
  • Therefore, the base or root form of the verb 'mend' should be used in place of the third-person present singular form of the verb 'mends'.
     

Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

Correct Sentence: He will lose all his wealth if he doesn't mend his ways.

Hinglish

  • रेखांकित खंड में, third-person present singular form of the verb का प्रयोग 'mends' गलत है।
  • 'Does' एक auxiliary verb or helping verb है जिसके बाद main verb होती है।
  • जब एक auxiliary verb होती है, तो main verb को tense के लिए चिह्नित करने की आवश्यकता नहीं होती है, क्योंकि tense को auxiliary में दिखाया जाता है।

  • इसलिए, base or root form of the verb 'mend' का प्रयोग third-person present singular form of the verb 'mends' के स्थान पर किया जाना चाहिए।
     

अत: सही उत्तर विकल्प 4 है ।

Key Points

  • In Active Voice, a sentence emphasizes the subject, performing an action.
  • In Passive Voice, a sentence emphasizes the action or the object of the sentence.
  • The given sentence is in the active voice and it is in the past simple tense.
  • When we convert this sentence into a passive voice, the subject ''They'' of the active voice becomes the object 'them', the object ''my phone'' becomes the subject.
  • The active format "V2 (did + repair)" should be converted into the passive format "was + V3 (repaired)".
  • This is the active and passive voice rule for the past simple tense.
     

Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

Additional Information

Verbs of passive format have a different set of tenses (*V3 - Past participle or Third form of the Verb) as given below in the table:

TENSE ACTIVE PASSIVE PASSIVE CONVERSION
Present Simple He plays football am/is/are + V3 Football is played by him
Present Continuous He is playing football am/is/are + being +V3 Football is being played by him
Present Perfect He has played football Has/have + been+ V3 Football has been played by him
Present Perfect Continuous He has been playing football Not used and unusual. Not used and unusual
Past Simple He played football Was/were + V3 Football was played by him
Past Continuous He was playing football Was/were + being + V3 Football was being played by him
Past Perfect He had played football Had + been + V3 Football had been played by him
Past Perfect Continuous He had been playing football Not used and unusual Not used and unusual
Future Simple He will play football Will + be + V3 Football will be played by him
Future Continuous He will be playing football Not used and unusual Not used and unusual
Future Perfect He will have played football Will have been + V3 Football will have been played by him
Future Perfect Continuous He will have been playing football Not used and unusual Not used and unusual
 

 

Hinglish

  • Active Voice में , एक वाक्य विषय पर जोर देता है, एक क्रिया करता है।
  • Passive Voice में , एक वाक्य वाक्य की क्रिया या वस्तु पर जोर देता है।
  • दिया गया वाक्य active voice में है और यह past simple tense में है।
  • जब हम इस वाक्य को passive voice में बदलते हैं, तो active voice का subject 'They', object 'them' बन जाता है और object 'my phone', subject बन जाता है।
  • Active format "V2 (did + repair)" को passive format "was + V3 (repaired)" में परिवर्तित किया जाना चाहिए।
  • यह past simple tense के लिए active and passive voice rule है।
     

अतः सही उत्तर विकल्प 2 है।
